review.causal_identification_verdict: Not established. The cloned-state design is the right identification strategy for the one-step projection effect, but it has not been executed. The longitudinal online/frozen reversal requires multi-round path dependence that the one-step design cannot identify. The exact-same-pool requirement is not met by the historical R3 runner. Causal identification is currently a design promise, not a result.
review.experiment_sufficiency_verdict: Zero. No scientific experiment has been run. The F0 artifacts are static substrate/provider/checkpoint qualifications with no scientific outcome. The historical R3 runner is not an executable R4 implementation. The decisive F2 experiment, the prospective F3 prediction, and the longitudinal F4 reversal are all unexecuted. A paper with zero executed scientific experiments is not sufficient for ICLR.

fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.cheapest_decisive_repair: Run the F2 cloned-state exact-same-pool projection-null experiment on a qualified substrate before any paper claim. This is one experiment, not a benchmark suite. If it fails directionally, STOP. If it passes, the paper becomes defensible as a mechanism study.
fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.issue: No scientific experiment has been run. The central causal claim—that changing g(T_K) while holding a(T_K), the pool, the updater, and the seed fixed changes future frozen skill—is entirely unverified. Every headline result (online/frozen reversal, projection rescue, prospective Gamma-times-delta prediction) is conditional on this unexecuted intervention. A paper built around an unrun decisive experiment is not a scientific contribution at ICLR level.

fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.cheapest_decisive_repair: Delete CADP as a named method. Demote it to an optional ablation. The only mechanism-derived intervention is Rejected-Witness, which is a one-line projection change, not a method. If Rejected-Witness suffices, the paper has no method contribution and must stand or fall on the mechanism.
fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.issue: CADP as a method is not novel after SkillCAT. Success/failure pairing, first-divergence extraction, contrastive skill editing, and replay validation are all already combined in SkillCAT's persistent external-skill pipeline. The dossier itself concedes this. The only residual is the serving-selection causal chain, which is not a method but a mechanism claim. Presenting CADP as a contribution would be a direct novelty overclaim.

fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.cheapest_decisive_repair: Remove all theorem-style presentation of the identity, the peak, the layer-cake extension, and the factorization. Present them as definitional tools and reference curves. The only theoretical claim that could survive is the prospective prediction that Gamma_K(p_z)*delta_z predicts held-out family sign and rank ordering, and that is an empirical claim requiring the unrun F3 experiment.
fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.issue: The central identity A_K - A_1 = V_pre - V_win = Gamma_K(Q) is a definitional equality, not a theorem. It holds for arbitrary joint distributions by construction of the rescue event. The i.i.d. peak p*(K) is an elementary order-statistic calculation. Neither can carry theoretical novelty. The Gamma-times-delta factorization is exact only under a gated projection that is identical outside the rescue event, making it a tautological decomposition whose content is entirely in the empirical sign and predictability of delta_z.

fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.cheapest_decisive_repair: Restrict all claims to the one-step projection effect until F4 multi-round streams are run. Do not assert the online/frozen reversal as a result. The cheapest repair is a claim-scope reduction, not an experiment.
fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.issue: The causal identification is not established by the design alone. The cloned-state intervention identifies the one-step projection effect only if the updater is deterministic given (S, g(T_K)) and the frozen evaluation is a valid proxy for future skill quality. Neither is verified. The longitudinal claim (online acting up, frozen skill down) requires multi-round path dependence that the one-step design cannot identify. The dossier's own Round-3 output concedes this: 'one-step identifies projection effect, not multi-round path-dependent evolution.'

fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.cheapest_decisive_repair: Write and test a new same-pool projection runner before any scientific provider call. This is a software artifact, not a scientific experiment, and is the cheapest possible repair.
fatal_or_verdict_changing_issues.issue: The old R3 runner is not an executable R4 implementation. It uses an independent K=1 shadow, not a same-pool precommitted rollout-0, and forbids nonselected failures from updater input. The dossier explicitly adjudicates this. Any paper written on the current artifacts would be describing an experiment that cannot be run as specified.

issues_not_worth_chasing: The information-theoretic statement I(Z; g_win(T_K)) <= I(Z; T_K). It is a vacuous data-processing inequality for a fixed LLM updater and should be deleted, not debated.
The continuous-verifier layer-cake identity. It is a standard representation that adds no empirical content unless a threshold policy is actually used. Not worth defending.

The i.i.d. Bernoulli intermediate-difficulty peak p*(K). It is an elementary order-statistic calculation under a one-parameter model and should be presented only as a reference curve. Not worth presenting as a law.
The topology-by-projection interaction (F5). It is downstream of the central mechanism and cannot rescue a paper whose core causal claim is unverified. Do not chase it before F2 passes.
The second substrate and backbone (F6). It is explicitly not responsible for saving the main conclusion and should not be requested as a repair.
review.novelty_after_skillcat_topocurate: The only surviving novelty is the mechanism-level claim that serving-time winner selection endogenously censors diagnostic failures from an external persistent updater, with an exact same-pool intervention that changes only the learning projection. This is not a method novelty (SkillCAT owns contrastive skill editing) and not a representation novelty (TopoCurate owns outcome-filtering discards branch structure). It is a narrow causal-identification claim about a specific coupling between acting and learning projections. Whether this rises to ICLR-level novelty depends entirely on the unrun F2 experiment showing a directional effect that SkillCAT-style contrast cannot explain without the serving-selection chain.
repairs_that_could_change_verdict: Run the single F2 cloned-state exact-same-pool projection-null experiment. This is the only experiment that can change the verdict from reject to revise. It requires one qualified substrate, one fixed skill state, one task batch, one K-pool, one updater, one seed, and arms differing only in g(T_K). If winner-only versus Rejected-Witness shows no directional frozen-skill difference on mixed rescue pools with positive estimated delta_z, the paper is dead. If it shows a directional effect, the paper becomes a narrow mechanism study with a real result.

Delete CADP and all method novelty claims. Reframe the paper as a mechanism-level causal study of serving-induced selective trajectory logging. The only intervention is Rejected-Witness. This removes the SkillCAT collision and forces the paper to stand on the causal chain, which is the only defensible residual.

Run a source-faithful SkillCAT-style contrast baseline on the same pools and updater. If it reproduces the full effect without the serving-selection causal chain, the paper is reduced to an application and should be stopped. This is a mandatory reduction baseline, not an optional ablation.

Freeze a mutually exclusive failure-family partition and the rejected-witness rule before outcomes. Without this, the prospective Gamma-times-delta prediction is unfalsifiable because overlapping post-hoc tags double-count mixed pools. This is a pre-registration repair, not an experiment.
review.single_sentence_verdict: R17 is a design document with a definitional identity, a method already reduced by SkillCAT, a representation claim already reduced by TopoCurate, and a central causal claim that depends entirely on a single unrun cloned-state projection-null experiment; without that experiment, the paper is not a scientific contribution and should be rejected.
review.strongest_reject_reason: The paper has no executed experiment, and its only defensible novelty is a mechanism-level causal claim that is currently indistinguishable from a definitional identity plus a selective-labeling instance. The decisive cloned-state projection-null experiment is the entire scientific content, and it has not been run. Without it, the paper is a design document with a method (CADP) already reduced by SkillCAT and a representation claim already reduced by TopoCurate.
review.theory_depth_verdict: Shallow. The core identity is definitional, the peak is an elementary order-statistic calculation, the layer-cake extension is standard, and the Gamma-times-delta factorization is tautological under the gated projection. The only substantive theoretical content is the prospective prediction that censoring mass times diagnostic advantage predicts held-out family sign and rank ordering, and that is an empirical claim requiring the unrun F3 experiment. The theory cannot carry the paper.
